discovery: Experimental demonstration of fractional charge and anyonic exchange statistics of quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall liquids

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Université, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases, fractional quantum Hall effect)
motivation: Anyons, particles that are neither bosons nor fermions, were predicted from topology in two dimensions in the 1970s and 1980s, and they are central to our understanding of topological order. The nominees made them experimental reality. Heiblum's shot-noise experiments directly measured the fractional charge e/3 of quasiparticles and later developed methods for probing their braiding. In 2020 Fève and co-workers used anyon collisions in a quantum Hall 'beam splitter' to extract the fractional exchange phase, and Manfra's group used heterostructures of exceptional quality and a Fabry-Pérot interferometer to observe braiding phase jumps of about 2π/3 at filling 1/3. Together these complementary experiments established that quasiparticles carry both fractional charge and fractional statistics, confirming a fundamentally new kind of quantum particle. They also opened the way to non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation.
